newsitem.title: USA: California income gap widens sharply - report.
newsitem.headline: California income gap widens sharply - report.

text.p: The income gap between California's highest and lowest wage earners has widened since early in the 1980s, according to a report Friday.
The California Franchise Tax Board said in the report that the highest income Californians, the top one percent, experienced an overall income increase of 42.3 percent from 1980 to the 1994 tax year.
The lowest 20 percent of the state's wage earners experienced a decrease of over 15 percent in the same period, the tax board said in its report.
The report contained data from 1980 through the 1994 tax year on adjusted gross income, which accounts for inflation and for tax law changes.
The Franchise Tax Board also found that some 68 percent of all taxpayers in the state make $40,000 or less annually. Only 1.3 percent of taxpayers make $200,000 or more per year.

"These figures describe more than income distribution," said Johan Klehs, Franchise Tax Board member and Board of Equalization chair. "It tells a disturbing story of the daily struggle of hard working wage earners who must labor even harder in order to make their financial ends meet."
"The information is important because the public and policy makers need to be aware of this factual analysis as we determine possible courses of action to bridge the income level gap," Klehs said.
